title: Bay-Area LLM Ops — compact field notes and follow-ups
content:
Quick context: attended the Bay Area LLM Ops meetup (half-day, Nov 2025). These are my handwritten-to-digital scratch notes: high-level takeaways, short paper links, and 3 small experiments I want to run on Redwood infra. Kept intentionally terse — meant for quick follow-up and to hand off to Dylan/Ava.

Highlights I cared about:
- Flash/attention kernel improvements are now commodity: everyone is doing kernel-level microbenchmarks (latency at short sequence lengths matters more than throughput in many customer flows).
- KV cache ergonomics + eviction policies are the quiet battleground: demo'd a prototype that exposes cache TTL + cost-weighted eviction; showed 15–20% tail latency reduction for chat workloads with skewed reuse.
- Model fallbacks: teams are shipping small model-family fallback graphs rather than single fallbacks (e.g., big->mid->tiny depending on cost/latency). Redwood routing ideas resonated.
- Observability: token-level traces + partial-apply logs (store prefix-match hits) are critical for diagnosing hallucination vs. perf regressions.

Notes on papers / demos called out (to read properly):
1) "FlashAttention 2-ish" talk — kernel optimizations for short tokens (slides referenced a new memory layout trick). Action: re-run our small-attn microbench with 128/256 seq lengths (paper link below).
2) "Adaptive KV eviction" — small demo, emphasized weighting by token frequency and LRU per-user buckets. Implementation sketch: maintain per-session recency + global frequency counter sampled every N requests.
3) "Fallback DAG for high availability" — product-y talk. Idea: route first to SKU A, fallback tries SKU B (cheaper), third try is cached prefix-only response. Consider adding route-level SLOs in Redwood console.

Immediate followups (3 quick experiments):
A) Microbench: FlashAttention kernel matrix comparison
- Goal: measure 95th P99 token latency at seq lengths 32/64/128 for gpt-like model on our dedicated nodes using serial vs fused kernels.
- Plan: small harness that runs 1k requests across controlled batch sizes (1,4,8). Record token-latency histogram, KV-store lookups, and GPU util.
- Owner: Dylan (I'll pair for runtimes).

B) KV eviction heuristic A/B (TTL + frequency sampling)
- Quick sim: replay 10k chat sessions from production trace (anonymized) to test eviction policies. Keep lightweight counters (1% sampled frequency).
- Metric: cache hit-rate, average tokens served from cache, and downstream cold-token latency.
- Risk: privacy checks — confirm dataset scrub with Security.

C) Fallback DAG smoke test on Canary route
- Build a simple 3-node routing policy: hosted-highperf -> hosted-cheap -> prefix-cache. Use canary rollout to 2% traffic.
- Observability: dashboard per-route (token cost, avg latency, error-rate).
- Success: maintain 99.5% of baseline quality measured by canned prompts.

Quick sketches / heuristics I want to remember:
- Eviction weight = alpha * freq + beta * recency_score + gamma * session_priority (simple linear score). Tune alpha:beta:gamma = 1:0.6:0.2 initially.
- For short-sequence workloads (<128 tokens), prefer single-sequence-optimized kernels even when throughput suffers — saves tail latency.
- Sampling for freq counters: reservoir sample per-user at 1% of requests to keep memory bounded.

Questions / open points:
- How much tail latency are we willing to trade for 20% cost savings in fallback flows? Need product input.
- Is there an existing production trace we can use for eviction sim, or do we ask CS for anonymized dump? (linked ENG ticket?).
- Monitoring: can we tag token-level traces with route-version and cache-hit boolean cheaply? Implementation cost estimate?

References & quick links (copy-paste later):
- Flash-attention / kernel notes: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.14135 (placeholder: I need to pull exact ref)
- Workshop slide deck (organizer): https://drive.example.com/llm-ops-bay-2025/slides
- Internal PR prototype for eviction counters: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-examples/pull/142
- ENG tracking: ENG-1423 (working thread on fallback DAG)

To-dos (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Pair with Dylan to get microbench harness running (target: reproduce basic numbers by EOD next week)
- [ ] Ping Security about anonymized trace availability (Ava)
- [ ] Draft a 1-pager for product on acceptable latency vs cost tradeoffs for fallbacks (Gina)

Random scribbles / heuristics to test experimentally later:
- Try small token prefetch on prefix matches: when prefix-match > 80% confidence, pre-run small 1-token batch to warm KV cache for next 4 tokens.
- Consider per-customer bucketed cache sizes (high-value customers get bigger per-session allocation).

Notes-to-self: keep this doc short. If we end up with a longer playbook, move to Confluence and link from ENG-1423.

End of notes.
